description:
Typical usage examples:

  Illumina data: python ardetype.py -i <batch_path> -m all
  Nanopore data: python ardetype.py -i <batch_path> -m all -ont

ARDETYPE is a modular bioinformatics pipeline for bacterial whole genome sequencing (WGS) analysis, designed for use in clinical microbiology, public health surveillance, and research settings. It supports both Illumina paired-end and Oxford Nanopore sequencing data.

The pipeline performs species-agnostic and species-specific analyses, integrating open-source tools to assess sequence quality, assemble genomes, classify organisms taxonomically, predict antimicrobial resistance (AMR), reconstruct plasmids, and generate structured reports. 

ARDETYPE is organized into four core modules:
  - bact_core: quality control, host read removal, genome assembly, taxonomic classification
  - bact_shell: assembly QC, AMR profiling, plasmid reconstruction and typing
  - bact_tip: species-specific subtyping
  - bact_shape: structured summarization of results

By combining established tools such as fastp, Kraken2, Shovill, QUAST, RGI, ResFinder, AMR++, and MOB-suite, ARDETYPE provides a comprehensive workflow for bacterial isolate characterization in high-stakes applications like outbreak investigation, resistance monitoring, and genomic epidemiology.
required_arguments:
Selects pipeline execution mode:

  all   - Run the complete pipeline on raw FASTQ files, including all analysis modules (bact_core, bact_shell, bact_tip, bact_shape).

  merge - Combine outputs from previous ARDETYPE runs located in one or more folders (see --merge_from),
	then generate unified reports under --output_dir.

arguments:
Path to directory that contains files to be analysed (files are NOT parsed from subfolders).
Check config_files/json/module_data/patterns/inputs section for expected input file extensions for bact_core module

Path to a custom pipeline configuration file in YAML format.
		If not provided, a default config file (config_files/yaml/config_modular_local.yaml) will be used.
		The configuration defines global parameters and tool-specific settings used during execution.

Directory where pipeline outputs will be saved. By default, it is set to '--input' as for most use cases it is recommended to ensure idempotent re-runs.
		In 'merge' mode, this must be specified explicitly as the destination for combined results.
Number of times Snakemake will attempt to rerun failed jobs. Helps recover from intermittent Network and/or I/O errors. Default is 3.
Maximum number of Snakemake jobs to run in parallel. Applies when executing on HPC. Default is 12.
flags:
Enable HPC execution mode.
With appropriate configuration, this allows submitting each pipeline module
(via subscripts/ardetype_jobscript.sh, --hpc, and -sm flags)
or per-sample job (via config_files/yaml/cluster.yaml and --hpc flag) to a cluster scheduler (PBS by default).
By default, the pipeline runs locally on the machine where the script is invoked.

Run each pipeline module as a separate HPC job. Snakemake sub-jobs are not submitted to the cluster in this mode.
Requires manual adjustment of subscripts/ardetype_jobscript.sh to control behavior. Effective only with --hpc.
Force rerun of all Snakemake rules across all pipeline modules, regardless of previous results or timestamps.
Disable output packing. By default, output files are organized into per-sample folders. Use this flag to keep a flat output directory structure.

Run the pipeline on a folder containing exclusively Nanopore reads (with _ONT.fastq.gz extension).
By default, the pipeline expects either Illumina data (_001.fastq.gz) alone or combined Illumina and Nanopore data.

Run the pipeline on a folder containing exclusively fasta input (with _contigs.fasta extension).
By default, the pipeline expects either Illumina data (_001.fastq.gz) alone or combined Illumina and Nanopore data.
nargs:
One or more paths to folders containing Ardetype output to be merged.
Allowed merge combinations: Hybrid + Hybrid, Illumina + Illumina, Nanopore + Nanopore.
Specify one or more Snakemake rule names (check snakefiles folder) to force rerun within the pipeline.
